memberTypes.label: Operators
memberTypes.definition: Directly operates a travel or hospitality business that serves consumers.
memberTypes.examples: Hotels, short-term rental hosts, property managers, tour operators, attractions, experience providers, DMCs.
memberTypes.criteria: Must actually operate a travel business that serves end consumers/travelers. Co-hosting consultants, virtual assistants, or service providers to operators do NOT qualify as operators.

memberTypes.label: Tech & Services
memberTypes.definition: Provides technology, software, tools, or professional services to the travel and hospitality industry.
memberTypes.examples: PMS, booking engines, channel managers, analytics platforms, AI tools for operators, consultants, agencies, revenue managers, marketing strategists, trainers, inspection software, claims management.
memberTypes.criteria: Serves the travel industry (primarily operators) in a B2B capacity. Includes both technology companies and professional service providers. Does NOT include consumer-facing platforms (those are Consumer Platforms).

memberTypes.label: Consumer Platforms
memberTypes.definition: Operates consumer-facing platforms, apps, websites, or tools that help travelers discover, plan, or book accommodations and experiences.
memberTypes.examples: Booking marketplaces (Airbnb, Booking.com, Expedia), metasearch engines, travel apps, travel websites, AI travel assistants, listing sites, price comparison tools, travel discovery platforms.
memberTypes.criteria: Consumers/travelers are the primary users, or equally important users alongside suppliers (as in marketplaces). The platform serves travelers directly, not just industry operators. If a company also provides B2B software alongside a consumer platform, it may qualify for both categories.

memberTypes.label: Creators & Media
memberTypes.definition: Produces content whose primary audience is consumers and travelers.
memberTypes.examples: Travel publishers, travel blogs, travel newsletters aimed at travelers, travel influencer brands, travel content creators.
memberTypes.criteria: The audience must be consumers/travelers, not the industry. Professionals who publish content as part of their B2B services (e.g., industry newsletters, educational content for operators) are Tech & Services, not Creators & Media.

memberTypes.label: Industry Organizations
memberTypes.definition: Organizations, conferences, and groups that convene, represent, or advocate for the travel and hospitality sector.
memberTypes.examples: Trade associations, DMOs/CVBs, tourism boards, regional alliances, industry conferences, professional networks.
memberTypes.criteria: Must be an organized body that convenes, represents, or advocates for travel industry participants. Not a commercial operator, technology provider, or content creator.

tags.description: Tags indicate which market segments a member serves. Members can have zero or more tags.
